games.title: Wąż
games.notes: Rules describe a line formation where the first player attempts to catch the last, with role rotation upon success.

games.title: Wilk i gąski
games.notes: Rules outline a chasing game with roles of 'wilk' (wolf) and 'gąski' (geese), including dialogue and role-switching mechanics.

games.title: Płótno
games.notes: Rules describe a game with roles like 'gospodynia' (hostess), 'złodziej' (thief), and 'płótno' (cloth), involving theft, counting, and role-based dialogue.

games.title: Ptaki (Farby)
games.notes: Rules describe a tag-like game with roles such as 'ptasznik' (birdkeeper) and 'kupiec' (merchant), including chasing mechanics and optional team-based endings.

games.title: Fabjan
games.notes: Rules outline a chasing game with roles like 'Fabjan' and 'starszy' (elder), involving dialogue, role-switching, and animal-themed naming.

games.title: Wójt i kuropatwy
games.notes: Rules describe a game with a seated line formation, dialogue, and a chasing mechanic where the 'wójt' (mayor) is pursued and roles rotate.

games.title: Żóraw
games.notes: Rules describe a circle-based game with a 'żóraw' (crane) guarding caps, involving singing, stealing, and tagging mechanics.

games.title: Czarny lud
games.notes: Rules outline a tag-based game with a 'czarny lud' (black folk) chasing others across a defined field, with captured players joining the chaser.

games.title: Na granicy
games.notes: Rules describe a team-based game with a 'król' (king) and two opposing groups crossing a 'pas graniczny' (border zone), involving tagging and role rotation.

games.title: Wójt
games.notes: Rules describe a simplified tag game with a 'wójt' (mayor) chasing others across a border zone, with role-switching upon capture.

games.title: Lis fantowy
games.notes: Rules outline a chasing game with a 'lis' (fox) and 'psy' (dogs), involving stealing an object, tagging, and forfeits (fanty).

games.title: Plinje
games.notes: Rules describe a team-based game with defined field boundaries, 'szranki' (lists), and 'więzienia' (prisons), attributed to Gołębiowski's description.
